title: Differential Power Analysis (DPA) — CPA in Miniature

questions.question: What is a “power trace” in side-channel analysis?
options: A measurement of device power consumption over time during computation
A log of ciphertexts produced by an algorithm
A proof that a key is random
A list of CPU cache misses
questions.explanation: A power trace records power usage over time; attackers use it as side-channel data.

questions.question: What does a leakage model attempt to predict?
options: How measured side-channel data relates to internal intermediate values
How to generate primes for RSA
How to compress ciphertexts
How to choose an IV for CBC
questions.explanation: A leakage model maps intermediates (e.g., bits) to expected leakage (e.g., power).

questions.question: In a classic AES CPA setup, which intermediate is often targeted for a 1-byte attack?
options: SBOX[plaintext_byte XOR key_byte]
The final ciphertext byte
The RSA modulus n
The IV used by CBC
questions.explanation: The first-round S-box output depends on one plaintext byte and one key byte.

questions.question: Why does correlation help recover the key byte in CPA?
options: The correct key guess makes predicted leakage align with measured leakage across traces
Correlation directly computes the secret key from one trace
Correlation removes the need for any model assumptions
Correlation works only when there is no noise
questions.explanation: The correct guess produces the strongest statistical relationship between prediction and observation.

questions.question: What does Hamming weight represent in a common leakage model?
options: The number of 1-bits in a byte/word value
The time to execute a loop
The number of cache sets in a CPU
The RSA public exponent
questions.explanation: Hamming weight is a simple proxy for switching activity that can correlate with power.

questions.question: What happens to CPA effectiveness if you add random noise to traces?
options: It typically needs more traces, but can still succeed if signal remains
It becomes impossible regardless of trace count
It always makes the key unrecoverable in theory
It turns CPA into a padding oracle attack
questions.explanation: Noise reduces SNR; collecting more traces can recover the signal by averaging.

questions.question: Which mitigation is most directly aimed at reducing power-analysis leakage?
options: Masking intermediate values with randomness
Using a longer ciphertext
Switching from CBC to ECB
Base64-encoding the plaintext
questions.explanation: Masking randomizes intermediates so leakage is less correlated with secrets.

questions.question: Why is side-channel security separate from mathematical cryptographic security?
options: Physical implementations can leak information through timing/power/EM/faults even when the math is sound
Side channels only apply to broken ciphers
Side channels only exist on old hardware
Side channels are prevented automatically by using HTTPS
questions.explanation: Security proofs assume black-box behavior; real devices leak through measurable phenomena.
